plain_description.what: Simulates shifts in the mix of question sources on held-out data. It compares two drift alarms tuned to the same false-alarm rate: a chi-square test on how questions fill the tree's cells, and the existing out-of-scope flag rate. It also compares the anchor-free tree's cells with k-means cells of the same number (no judge calls).
plain_description.why: It tests whether the cells are useful for monitoring, by detecting when incoming traffic changes, and whether a tree does this better than plain clustering.
plain_description.information: If watching cell occupancy beats the out-of-scope rate, cells add a practical monitoring use; a tree beating k-means would favour the tree. Result: on synthetic shifts of moderate size, the cell-occupancy alarm detects more often than the out-of-scope rate (61% vs 21%). This comes from small sources whose share is multiplied, not from pure cells, and the out-of-scope rate is blind by construction to some directions. The tree's cells do no better than k-means (no equivalence claimed). Small shifts were not detected. The shifts are synthetic, not real traffic.
